hindi: वह मैथुन में केवल वात को छोड़ता है।
english: In sexual union it releases only Vāta (wind-humour).
notes: Subject 'tat' is carried from the preceding unit (not in this chunk); what 'it' refers to is not stated here. Vāta is kept as the humour (doṣa); the line does not say whether plain 'wind' is meant.

hindi: जब वह पूरी तरह हानि पहुँचाता है, या हानि न पहुँचाते हुए ही स्रोत के मुख को ढक देता है,
english: When, however, it wholly damages, or, without damaging, simply closes the mouth of the channel (srotas),
notes: Subject not stated in the line (carried from earlier context, not in this chunk). GROUPING: 78 and 79 appear to form one 'yadā ... tadā' sentence. 'upahaṃti' is the printed spelling of upahanti. srotas (channel) is kept as a doctrinal term.

hindi: तब वह संस्कार से बाहर हो जाता है। वहाँ संस्कार है: वाजीकर बस्तियाँ यानी वाजीकर एनिमा, अभ्यवहार और चित्त को हर्षित करने वाले भी।
english: Then (he) becomes outside refining treatment (saṃskāra). There the treatment is aphrodisiac (vājīkara) enemas (basti), internal administration (abhyavahāra), and mind-gladdening (ones) too.

text_flags.why: possible: a stray space splits 'harṣaṇāni' (n. nom. pl. 'gladdening'); sense and the following 'ca' fit one word

notes: The subject of 'bhavati' is not stated. 'saṃskārabāhya' is read 'outside (the scope of) refining treatment'; the sense 'treatment' for saṃskāra is taken from 'tatra saṃskāraḥ'. 'vājīkarā bastayaḥ' is regular sandhi (visarga dropped before b). The list is: aphrodisiac enemas, internal administration, and gladdening (ones). 'basti' = enema here.

english: When a man of little seed and little strength, agitated, possessed of aversion to women, or desiring another, causes an obstruction of intercourse with the woman, or the woman is of that kind towards the man,

hindi: तब आसेक्य। स्त्री और पुरुष वैसे ही प्रकार के हो जाते हैं। तब वह वक्रध्वज यानी टेढ़े शिश्न वाला हो जाता है; उसका ध्वज यानी शिश्न कभी कड़ा नहीं होता।
english: Then āsekya. The woman and the man become of that kind. Then he becomes vakradhvaja (one with a bent dhvaja, the penis); his dhvaja (penis) is simply not made stiff.
notes: GROUPING: 82 appears to continue 81. 'tadā''sekyaṃ' (double avagraha as printed) is read tadā + āsekyam; āsekya appears to be a technical name but the line does not define it, so it is left untranslated and the reading is not firm. 'dhvaja' (banner) is a euphemism for the penis (standard). 'vakradhvaja' is read as a bahuvrīhi naming a type. The 'then ... he' clauses have no stated subject.

hindi: जब दुर्गन्धयुक्त योनि वाली स्त्री का गर्भ होता है,
english: When an embryo (garbha) arises of a woman with a putrid vagina (yoni),

notes: 'pūti' means putrid or foul-smelling; the line does not say which. The printed 'striyā' is instrumental, kept in `gram`; the translation follows the genitive reading. GROUPING: 83 and 84 appear to belong together (84 supplies the result), the subject of 84 is not stated.

hindi: उस शुक्र के आस्वाद से ध्वज यानी शिश्न का उठना पाता है।
english: From tasting that semen (śukra) he gets the raising of the dhvaja (penis).
notes: Unsandhied print 'āsvādāt dhvaja' (final t not changed to d); recorded as a print habit, not flagged. Subject 'he' is not stated. 'ucchrāya' = raising, erection (probable).

hindi: जब पुमुरुभावपि तत्सौगंधिकारण्यं — ये छपे रूप अस्पष्ट हैं और अनुमानित पाठ पर ही कुछ कहा जा सकता है — तब योनि और ध्वज की गन्ध से बल पाता है।
english: When 'pumurubhāvapi tatsaugaṃdhikāraṇyaṃ' (printed forms unclear; on a conjectural reading only), he obtains strength from the smell of the yoni and the dhvaja.

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: 'pumuru-' is not a word; 'pumān ubhau api' is only a guess

notes: The second and third words of the line are doubtful in print; no firm reading is built on them. The subject of 'labhate' is not stated. 'yonidhvajagandhena' is read as smell of the yoni and the dhvaja (dvandva); 'smell of the dhvaja of the yoni' is also possible. 'dhvaja' = penis (standard euphemism). hindi: जब ईर्ष्या से अभिभूत, मन्द हर्ष वाले दोनों संयुक्त होते हैं, तब ईर्ष्यालु यह संज्ञा

words.gloss: of the male, of the man

hindi: जब पुरुष गर्भ में वायु और अग्नि के दोष से वृषण यानी अण्डकोष का नाश होता है, तब वह वायुपिण्डक नाम वाला होता है।
english: When, in the male embryo, there is destruction of the testes (vṛṣaṇa) through the fault of wind (vāyu) and fire (agni), then (it) becomes the one called vāyupiṇḍaka.
notes: 'puruṣasya garbhasya' is read 'of the male embryo'; the line does not say 'in' but the genitive carries it. 'doṣa' here is read 'fault' (not the humour), because it is joined with agni and vāyu in a compound. vṛṣaṇa = testis (standard); the plural or dual is not marked in the compound. 'vāyupiṇḍaka' is a type name, left untranslated. Subject of 'bhavati' not stated.

hindi: कर्म की विचित्रता से ये आठ षण्ढ-योनियाँ यानी नपुंसकों की आठ प्रकार की उत्पत्तियाँ संकीर्ण यानी मिश्रित कही गई हैं।
english: These eight kinds (yoni) of ṣaṇḍha (the impotent), because of the variety of action (karma), are said to be mixed.
notes: Printed 'ṣaṃḍha' is an orthographic form of ṣaṇḍha (recorded once, not flagged). 'saṃkīrṇāḥkathitāḥ' is printed as one token without the expected space. 'yoni' is read as 'kind/origin'. 'Mixed' (saṃkīrṇa) may also be read 'miscellaneous'. The text does not here list the eight.

hindi: जब स्त्री के रक्त और गर्भाशय को दोष थोड़ा दूषित करते हैं, तब जो गर्भ होता है, उस गर्भ के माता से उत्पन्न जिस-जिस अवयव के बीज में या बीजांश में दोष प्रकोप को प्राप्त होता है, उस-उस अवयव में विकृति प्रवेश करती है।
english: When, however, the doṣas slightly vitiate the woman's blood (śoṇita) and uterus (garbhāśaya), then in the embryo that comes to be, whichever mother-born part (avayava) of that embryo has its doṣa reach provocation in the seed (bīja) or in the seed-portion, into that very part a deformity (vikṛti) enters.
notes: 'mātṛjasyāvayavasya' is genitive, read as the possessor of the seed or seed-portion. Doctrinal terms doṣa, bīja, avayava are kept. 'garbhāśaya' = uterus (standard). Constructions 'yasya yasya ... tam tam' are distributive ('each such part').

hindi: जब इसके गर्भाशय में स्थित शोणित नामक बीज में निर्वर्तक बीज दूषित होता है, तब वह बन्ध्या को उत्पन्न करता है।
english: When, indeed, in her seed called blood (śoṇita), situated in the uterus (garbhāśaya), the forming seed (nirvartaka bīja) is vitiated, then it produces a barren one (vandhyā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ra' appears inserted ('ākhye' = called); the same insertion is seen in 'śukarārakhye' (97); 'śoṇita-ākhye' fits the sense

notes: Token 'yadā hyasyāḥ' = yadā + hi + asyāḥ. The subject of 'janayati' is not stated ('it', the vitiated seed). 'Barren (vandhyā)' is the feminine as printed; the noun 'woman' is not in the text. 'nirvartaka' = that which brings about or forms (the body), the line does not say more. The two uses of 'bīja' (the blood-seed, and the forming seed) are as printed.

hindi: जब उसका अवयव, तब — छपा रूप तदापूतप्रजां अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ पर बिगड़ी हुई सन्तान वाली —
english: When its part (avayava), then, on a conjectural reading, (one) of spoiled offspring (pūtiprajā) —

text_flags.why: possible: 'āpūtaprajāṃ' is not a word; 'pūtiprajam' occurs in 97 and the sense 'one whose offspring spoils' fits 93; the clause also lacks a predicate

notes: Damaged or elliptical: 'yadā tasya avayavaḥ' has no predicate, and 'tadāpūtaprajāṃ' is doubtful in print. The verb 'janayati' (produces) is understood from 91, but is not supplied in the translation. GROUPING: 92 appears to continue 91 and be completed by 93. 'pūtiprajā' as 'one whose offspring is spoiled' is a conjecture, not firm.

hindi: जब फिर वह अवयव और स्त्री को बनाने वालों के, तथा शरीर में आश्रित अधोगुरुता आदि के निर्माता जो बीजांश हैं, उनका एक देश,
english: When again that part (avayava), and the seed-portions (bījāṃśa) which produce the female-making (ones) and the body-dependent (ones) beginning with downward heaviness — a part of those,

hindi: उसे स्त्रीव्यापद् कहते हैं।

words.gloss: mṛṇāsuliṅgā (a name; printed form kept, meaning unclear)

hindi: इसी प्रकार पुरुष के विषय में भी, जब शुक्र नामक बीज में बीज दूषित होता है, इत्यादि जोड़ लेना चाहिए: बन्ध्य, बिगड़ी हुई सन्तान वाला, तथा पुरुष की आकृति की प्रधानता वाला, अपुरुष, जिसका नाम मृणासुलिंगा है, उसे उत्पन्न करता है। इसके द्वारा, माता से और पिता से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति के व्याख्यान से, सात्म्य से, रस से और सत्त्व से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति भी समझा दी गई होती है।
english: In just the same way, for a man: 'when, in the seed called śukra, the seed is vitiated' and so on, one should apply it: a barren (one), one of spoiled offspring; and likewise (one) mostly of male shape, a non-male, named mṛṇāsuliṅgā, it produces. By this explanation of the deformity of the mother-born and father-born parts, the deformity of the parts born of sātmya (what suits), of rasa and of sattva (mind) is explained too.

text_flags.why: possible: 'śukarāra-' is not a word; 'śukra-ākhye' (called semen) fits the sense and the pattern of 'śoṇitākhye' in 91; the ra-insertion also appears there

notes: The first part is a quotation ('when ... iti') of the pattern of 91, applied to the man. 'mṛṇāsuliṅgā' is a name after 'nāma'; its meaning is unclear and the print may be corrupt, so it is left untranslated. Several tokens are printed without spaces (bījaṃpraduṣyatītyādiyojayedvaṃdhyaṃ, puruṣākṛtiprāyamapuruṣaṃmṛṇāsuliṃgā, cāvayavānāṃvikṛtivyākhyānena). 'vandhyam' is read as an accusative object (a barren male), 'pūtiprajam' as 'of spoiled offspring' (conjectural). sātmya = what suits one, habit; rasa here is nutritive fluid (probable); sattva = mind (standard); each tagged as the standard reading. Subject of 'janayati' not stated. 'ity-etena' closes the quotation and starts 'by this'.

hindi: जिस अंग-अवयव के बीज में या बीजांश में उत्पत्ति होती है, उस-उस अंग-अवयव की विकृति उत्पन्न होती है।
english: Of whichever limb-part (aṅga-avayava), in its seed or seed-portion, an origin occurs, of that very limb-part a deformity arises.

words.gloss: dull, stupid (jaḍa); deaf; mute; nasal-voiced (minmiṇa; probable); stammering; lame; hunchbacked; dwarfish; deficient; limb; excessive; limb; -ness

hindi: और जब गर्भ पाई हुई स्त्री — अनक्षम् छपा रूप अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ पर निरन्तर — वातकारक पदार्थों का सेवन करती है, तब उसका प्रकुपित वायु शरीर में सरकता हुआ गर्भाशय में ठहरकर गर्भ में जड़ता, बहरापन, गूँगापन, नकियापन, हकलापन, लंगड़ापन, कुबड़ापन, बौनापन, अंगों की कमी और अंगों की अधिकता, या कोई दूसरा वात का विकार उत्पन्न करता है।
english: And when (she) who has obtained a pregnancy resorts only to Vāta-increasing (ones), the printed 'anakṣam' being unclear (conjecturally 'constantly'), then her provoked Vāyu, moving along the body and lodging in the uterus (garbhāśaya), produces in the embryo the states of being dull (jaḍa), deaf (badhira), mute (mūka), nasal-voiced (minmiṇa), stammering (gadgada), lame (khañja), hunchbacked (kubja), dwarfish (vāmana), deficient in limbs and excessive in limbs, or another Vāta disorder (vātavikāra).

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: 'anakṣam' is not a word in this sense; 'aniśam' (constantly) is a guess from similar letters (śa/kṣa)

notes: The word 'anakṣam' is doubtful; the conjecture 'aniśam, constantly' is not built into the Sanskrit and is only marked in the translation. 'labdhagarbhā' = having obtained an embryo (pregnant). 'garbhasya' goes with the long compound ('in the embryo ... states of ...'); the suffix -tva applies to the whole list. 'minmiṇa' (nasal or indistinct speech) is probable. 'hīnāṅga' (deficient in limbs) and 'adhikāṅga' (excessive in limbs) are as printed. Vāyu is Vāta (standard).
